chapters.title: The Lost Pages
chapters.focus: present simple · there is / there are · can

pages.text: This is {hero}. {hero} has a little pet called {pet}. They live in a small house near the [[meadow|a big field with grass and flowers]]. Today the sun is warm. The flowers are yellow and white.

q.explain: “They live in a small house near the meadow.”

pages.text: In the morning, {hero} sees an old book on the grass. It is big and blue. There are gold stars on it. But the book is sad. Its pages are [[gone|not there any more]]!

q.explain: “It is big and blue.” The stars on it are gold, but the book is blue.

pages.text: “Hello,” says the book. “I am the Starlight Storybook. The wind takes my pages. There are six pages, in six [[realms|lands or kingdoms in a story]]. Can you help me?”

q.q: How many pages does the book need?
q.explain: “There are six pages, in six realms.”

pages.text: {hero} looks at {pet}. {pet} jumps up and down. “Yes, we can help!” says {hero}. Under a big pink flower, {pet} finds the first page. It is [[shiny|bright, like a star]]. The book smiles.

q.explain: “Under a big pink flower, {pet} finds the first page.”

options: a field of grass and flowers
final.explain: A meadow is a big field with grass and flowers.

chapters.title: Picnic in the Meadow
chapters.focus: present simple · there is / there are · can · like

pages.text: Today {hero} and {pet} have a picnic in the meadow. There is a red and white [[blanket|a big soft cloth you sit on or sleep under]] on the grass. In the basket there are sandwiches and ten red strawberries. {pet} likes strawberries very much.

q.explain: “{pet} likes strawberries very much.”

notes.sandwiches: The sandwiches are in the basket, but the story says “{pet} likes strawberries very much.”
notes.the red blanket: The blanket is for sitting on. The story says “{pet} likes strawberries very much.”
notes.the grass: The blanket is on the grass. The story says “{pet} likes strawberries very much.”

pages.text: Then {hero} sees a little white rabbit in the tall grass. The rabbit is [[shy|a bit scared to talk to new friends]]. It can see the strawberries, but it cannot come close. “Hello, little rabbit,” says {hero}. “You can have a strawberry too.”

q.q: Why does the rabbit stay in the grass?
q.explain: “The rabbit is shy.” Shy animals stay away from new friends.

The story never says it is angry. It says “The rabbit is shy.”
It CAN see the food: “It can see the strawberries, but it cannot come close.”
A sleeping rabbit can't see anything, but this one can: “It can see the strawberries.”

pages.text: The rabbit hops to the blanket. It eats one strawberry, then two, then three! Now the rabbit is happy. But then the sky is grey, and there are big [[raindrops|small drops of water that fall from the sky]]. Oh no, rain!

q.q: How many strawberries does the rabbit eat?
q.explain: “It eats one strawberry, then two, then three!”

notes.one: One is only the start: “one strawberry, then two, then three!”
notes.two: Two is not the end: “…then two, then three!”
notes.ten: There are ten strawberries in the basket, but the rabbit eats three.

pages.text: {hero}, {pet} and the rabbit run under a big tree. They can hear the rain on the leaves. Soon the rain stops and the sun comes out. Look! There is a [[rainbow|a curve of colours in the sky after rain]] over the meadow. “This is the best picnic!” says {hero}.

q.q: Where do they go when it rains?
q.explain: “{hero}, {pet} and the rabbit run under a big tree.”

notes.into the house: The house is near the meadow, but they don't go there. They “run under a big tree.”
notes.into the tall grass: The rabbit came from the tall grass, but now they all “run under a big tree.”
notes.under the blanket: The blanket stays on the grass. They “run under a big tree.”

options: colours in the sky after rain
a big soft cloth you sit on at a picnic
drops of water from the sky
final.explain: A rainbow is a curve of colours in the sky after the rain.

notes.a big soft cloth you sit on at a picnic: That's a blanket, the soft cloth they sit on.
notes.a little white rabbit: That's the shy new friend in the grass.
notes.drops of water from the sky: Those are raindrops. The rainbow comes after the raindrops stop.

chapters.title: The Bunny's Tea Party
chapters.focus: present simple · there is / there are · can · like

pages.text: The next day the white rabbit comes back. “Please come to my [[burrow|a small hole under the ground where a rabbit lives]],” it says. {hero} and {pet} follow. There is a tiny table with four cups.

q.explain: “Please come to my burrow.” A burrow is a rabbit's home under the ground.

notes.in a tall tree: Rabbits do not live in tall trees. The rabbit says “come to my burrow.”
notes.in the picnic basket: The picnic basket is for food. The rabbit's home is a burrow.
notes.in a big house: There is no big house here. The rabbit lives in a burrow.

pages.text: The rabbit can pour tea. The tea smells like honey. {pet} likes the sweet tea. {hero} likes the daisy flowers. There is a small [[cake|a sweet food you bake]] on a pink plate.

q.explain: “{pet} likes the sweet tea.”

notes.the daisy flowers: {hero} likes the daisy flowers. The story says “{pet} likes the sweet tea.”
notes.the pink plate: The cake is on the pink plate. {pet} likes the sweet tea.
notes.the bush: They came to the burrow, but {pet} likes the sweet tea.

pages.text: The rabbit opens a little box. Inside there are three shiny [[acorns|the hard seeds of an oak tree]]. “These are gifts,” it says. “You can keep one each.” {pet} hops with joy.

q.q: How many acorns are in the box?
q.explain: “Inside there are three shiny acorns.”

notes.one: They each keep one, but the box has three in total.
notes.four: There are four cups on the table, not four acorns.
notes.ten: There were ten strawberries at the picnic, not ten acorns.

pages.text: After tea the sun is warm. “Thank you,” says {hero}. “This is a lovely party.” The rabbit is not [[shy|a bit scared to talk to new friends]] now. It waves goodbye. {pet} waves too.

q.q: How does the rabbit feel at the end?
options: It is asleep in the box.
It is lost in the meadow.
q.explain: “The rabbit is not shy now.” It waves goodbye happily.

The story never says it is angry. It waves goodbye.
The acorns were in the box. The rabbit waves goodbye.
They are at the burrow, not lost. The rabbit waves goodbye.

options: a small hole under the ground where a rabbit lives
a sweet food you bake for a party
a hard seed of an oak tree
final.explain: A burrow is a rabbit's underground home.

notes.a sweet food you bake for a party: That's a cake, the sweet food on the pink plate.
notes.a hard seed of an oak tree: Those are acorns, the shiny gifts.
notes.a cup for drinking tea: That's a cup. The burrow is the rabbit's home.

chapters.title: The Star Path Home
chapters.focus: present simple · there is / there are · can · like

pages.text: After the tea party the white rabbit walks with {hero} and {pet}. There is a soft path of tiny [[stars|little bright lights in the sky]] on the grass. The stars glow. {pet} can hop from star to star.

options: a soft path of tiny stars
q.explain: “There is a soft path of tiny stars on the grass.”

notes.a big boat: There is no boat here. The story says a soft path of tiny stars.
notes.a cold river: There is no cold river on the grass. There is a star path.
notes.a tall school: They are in the meadow, not at a school. There is a star path.

pages.text: The rabbit gives {hero} a little [[parcel|a small wrapped gift]]. “This is for your home,” it says. Inside there is a shiny acorn and a daisy. {hero} likes the gift. {pet} likes the daisy smell.

q.explain: “The rabbit gives {hero} a little parcel.”

notes.a cup of cold tea: Tea was at the party. Now the rabbit gives a little parcel.
notes.a picnic basket of jam: The picnic was another day. Today the gift is a little parcel.
notes.a new burrow key: There is no burrow key. The rabbit gives a little parcel.

pages.text: They can follow the star path home. There are [[fireflies|tiny bugs that glow with yellow light at night]] too. The fireflies like to dance. {pet} can see the yellow lights. “Thank you,” says {hero}. “We like your path.”

q.explain: “{pet} can see the yellow lights.”

notes.a dark cave: There is no dark cave. {pet} can see the yellow lights.
notes.a lost sock: Nobody lost a sock. {pet} can see the yellow lights.
notes.a blue bus: There is no bus in the meadow. {pet} can see the yellow lights.

pages.text: At the end of the path the stars go soft. The rabbit is happy. It is not [[shy|a bit scared to talk to new friends]] now. It waves. {hero} and {pet} wave too. Home feels warm. There is a smile on every face.

q.q: How does the rabbit feel now?
q.explain: The rabbit is happy and “It is not shy.” It waves goodbye.

notes.angry and loud: It waves happily. The story does not say it is angry.
notes.lost and cold: They know the path home. The rabbit is not lost.
notes.asleep in the parcel: The parcel is a gift. The rabbit waves; it is not asleep in it.

options: a path of tiny stars on the grass
final.explain: A parcel is a small wrapped gift — the one with the acorn and daisy.

notes.a path of tiny stars on the grass: That's the star path, not a parcel.
notes.a cup of honey tea: Tea was earlier; a parcel is a wrapped gift.

chapters.title: The Thank-You Acorn
chapters.focus: present simple · there is / there are · can · like

pages.text: The next morning {hero} opens the little [[parcel|a small wrapped gift]]. There is the shiny acorn and the daisy. {pet} can smell the daisy. “We like this gift,” says {hero}. “We can say thank you.”

options: a shiny acorn and a daisy
a cold cup of honey tea from the party
a big blue boat for the river
a hard school book about oaks
q.explain: “There is the shiny acorn and the daisy.”

notes.a cold cup of honey tea from the party: Tea was at the party. Inside the parcel are the acorn and the daisy.
notes.a big blue boat for the river: There is no boat in the parcel. There is a shiny acorn and a daisy.
notes.a hard school book about oaks: There is no school book. The gift is a shiny acorn and a daisy.

pages.text: There is soft moss under an oak tree. {hero} can dig a tiny hole. {pet} can drop the shiny [[acorn|the hard seed of an oak tree]] in. They cover it with earth. “Grow well,” whispers {hero}.

q.q: Where do they put the acorn?
options: in a tiny hole under an oak
in a cup of honey tea from the party
in a picnic basket full of jam tarts
in a dark cave by the cold river
q.explain: They dig a tiny hole under an oak and drop the acorn in.

notes.in a cup of honey tea from the party: Tea is for drinking. The acorn goes in a tiny hole under the oak.
notes.in a picnic basket full of jam tarts: The picnic basket is not here. They plant the acorn under the oak.
notes.in a dark cave by the cold river: There is no cave. The acorn goes in a tiny hole under the oak.

pages.text: The white rabbit comes hop, hop. It likes the planted acorn. There are three little [[ribbons|thin soft strips of cloth for tying gifts]] in its bag. “These are thank-you ribbons,” it says. {pet} can wear one. {hero} can wear one too.

q.explain: “There are three little ribbons in its bag.”

notes.a loud drum: There is no drum. The rabbit brings three little ribbons.
notes.a lost sock: Nobody lost a sock. The rabbit brings thank-you ribbons.
notes.a cold river: There is no river gift. The rabbit brings three little ribbons.

pages.text: They tie a ribbon on the oak. There is a smile on every face. “Thank you for the star path and the parcel,” says {hero}. The rabbit is happy. It is not [[shy|a bit scared to talk to new friends]]. {pet} likes the warm sun.

q.explain: The rabbit is happy and “It is not shy.”

notes.angry and loud: It smiles with them. The story does not say it is angry.
notes.lost in the parcel: They are under the oak together. The rabbit is not lost.
notes.asleep in the moss: The rabbit stands and smiles; it is not asleep in the moss.

options: the hard seed of an oak tree
a thin thank-you ribbon for tying gifts
a soft glowing path of tiny stars
a warm cup of honey tea
final.explain: An acorn is the hard seed of an oak — the shiny gift they planted.

notes.a soft glowing path of tiny stars: That's the star path from earlier.

chapters.title: The Little Sprout
chapters.focus: present simple · there is / there are · can · like

pages.text: A few soft days later {hero} walks back to the oak. There is a tiny green [[sprout|a very small new plant]] in the moss. {pet} can see two little leaves. “We like this sprout,” says {hero}. “It can grow.”

q.q: What do they see in the moss?
options: a cold cup of honey tea
q.explain: “There is a tiny green sprout in the moss.”

notes.a cold cup of honey tea: Tea is not in the moss. There is a tiny green sprout.
notes.a big blue boat: There is no boat. There is a tiny green sprout.
notes.a hard school book: There is no school book. There is a tiny green sprout.

pages.text: There is a small watering can by the rabbit's bag. {hero} can tip a little water on the earth. {pet} can smell the wet moss. The white rabbit hops over. It likes the [[gentle|soft and kind, not rough]] water. “Not too much,” it says with a smile.

q.q: What does {hero} do with the watering can?
options: tips a little water on the earth
fills a boat with cold tea
hides the ribbons in a cave
q.explain: “{hero} can tip a little water on the earth.”

notes.fills a boat with cold tea: There is no boat of tea. They water the sprout gently.
notes.hides the ribbons in a cave: The ribbons stay on the oak. They water the sprout.
notes.paints a hard school book: There is no school book. They tip a little water on the earth.

pages.text: There are three friends under the oak now: {hero}, {pet}, and the rabbit. They can sit on soft moss. They like to share a quiet oak day. The rabbit brings a tiny [[picnic|a small outdoor meal]] of carrot sticks. “We can thank the sprout too,” laughs {hero}.

q.q: Who sits under the oak together?
options: only a loud drum from town
a lost sock and a cold river
q.explain: “There are three friends under the oak now: {hero}, {pet}, and the rabbit.”

notes.only a loud drum from town: There is no drum picnic. The three friends sit together.
notes.a lost sock and a cold river: No sock or river joins them. The three friends sit under the oak.
notes.Crumb from the candy bakery: Crumb is in Candy Village. Here the rabbit shares the oak day.

pages.text: The sun is warm. There is a ribbon on the oak and a sprout in the moss. {pet} likes the quiet. “We can come again,” says {hero}. The rabbit is happy. It is not shy. Oak day feels [[cosy|warm, soft and safe]].

q.explain: Oak day feels cosy; they like the quiet warm sun.

notes.angry and loud: They smile together. The story does not say it is angry.
notes.lost in a dark cave: They are under the oak, not lost in a cave.
notes.asleep in a cold river: Nobody is asleep in a river. Oak day feels cosy.

options: a thin thank-you ribbon for tying gifts
a warm cup of honey tea
a hard seed still inside a parcel
final.explain: A sprout is a very small new plant — the tiny green leaves above the planted acorn.

notes.a hard seed still inside a parcel: The acorn was the seed; the sprout is the new plant.
